neural_arm.notes: Scored raw suggestions (empty = abstain, no baseline fallback, min_confidence 0.0). Same run's static/fused arms reproduced identical accuracy (decoder 0.790554, fused 0.777207); absolute latencies drift with machine load and are not restated. The neural route decodes from the model + vocabulary under pinyin constraints, so it is NOT bounded by gold_in_top10_coverage (0.810062) — it bypasses the frozen Rime Top-10 ceiling entirely. ~286s wall time for 974 samples (~0.29s/sample, model loaded once): eval-grade latency, not yet interactive (Phase 2 需要 4-bit 引擎).

fused_latency_cache.change: rimeai_daemon/fused_lm.py: interpolation weights and per-domain count stores resolved once per FusedCharLM instance (was per scoring call); per-instance memo of next_char_log_prob keyed by (context[-max_context_characters:], character), capped at 16384 entries (>1.7x the worst-case unique keys of one max-length decode); result-preserving because every backoff gram of both layers ends at the scored position. No module-level caches; one instance lives one request.

latency_budget.note: after weight hoisting + memoization the fused arm still exceeds decoder-only p95 by 1.472459 ms (was 2.554916 ms); absolute latencies of both arms dropped versus the first measurement (machine load differs), so the delta is the comparable figure. Fused accuracy and decision counts are identical to the uncached run, confirming the cache is result-preserving.

cache_hit_rate.finding: instrumented re-decode of the same 974 test samples: beam search produces ~99.5% unique (context, character) keys per request (repeats come almost only from the baseline _sequence_score overlap), so memoization alone cannot meet the +1 ms budget; the residual cost is the inherent second backoff walk (user global layer) plus exp/log per scored position. Escalated for an architecture ruling; no beam-width or partial-fusion changes made here.

fused_final_path_adjudication.change: Controller Ruling 10: beam expansion in BeamSentenceDecoder.raw_decode now always scores with the default static scorer; the scorer argument is used only for final-path adjudication — margin = sequence score of the statically-decoded winning path minus the baseline's, both under the provided scorer (scorer=None keeps the static path byte-identical). FusedCharLM's per-instance memo cache was removed: final-path scoring makes only ~2×sentence-length mostly-unique calls per request, and the cache had measured a 0.5% hit rate even on the far denser expansion-time call pattern. The construction-time weight/count hoist stays.
fused_final_path_adjudication.accuracy_note: fused_sentence_accuracy 0.777207 vs decoder 0.790554 (−1.335 pt; −1.643 pt with expansion-time fusion, superseded): fusion now shifts only margins/gating, never the decoded path. The residual gap is fused margins pushing 43 static suggestions below the frozen threshold (below_threshold 200 vs 157; suggestion 125 vs 168) — a threshold recalibration question, not a path-quality question. no_change counts are identical (649), confirming the decoded texts are exactly the static arm's.

supersedes.stage: expansion-time fusion + weight hoist + memo cache (fused_latency_cache)
